
# Course Goals 
(as of 10/10)
Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

- explain the social and ethical context in which software and video games are developed, marketed, and used;
- describe the technologies and platforms upon which modern interactive software and video games are built;
- apply software engineering concepts necessary to develop video games within a development team;
- analyze the computational theory used in game design and related fields of computer science (artificial intelligence, computer graphics, networks, etc.);
- apply game theory to multi-player games, decision-making, and artificial intelligence.


Game design vs game development: course split into two blocks.


# Course Structure:

## Block A: game design
Baseline with games that already exist for specific examples. 
Dive into specific games (tutorial walktrough).

- Week 1: history of games, game loop + mechanics, game engine intro
- Week 2: implementing mechanics + tutorials (labs)
- Codebase: tutorials (assets preloaded) + finished example for inspiration?
- Block A exam: Thursday 1/13
- Block A project: Friday paper game jam
    - restriction:

## Block B: game dev
- Week 3: ideation, prototypes, character design
- Week 4: level design, balance, playtesting
- Codebase: template for given genre?, or use tutorial as example?
- Block B exam: Thursday 1/28
- Block B project: *genre* game jam + pitch
    - couch co-op, top-down (Overcooked). skeleton code.
    - restrictions: activity to pick three restrictions for each group.

## Group Roles:
For each, identify objectives and metrics.
Average salary role in midwest.
What questions should be asked in an interview (start of block B).

- Technical Art: program shader tech or particle system, assets.
- Game Play Engineer: networking or mechanics.
- Game Design: system for spawning or enemy attack.
- Producer/QA: pitch, schedules, meeting notes, community management, bug management.

## Course Topics
### Week 1: Game Design Introduction
history of games, game loop + mechanics, game engine intro

- History of games: 1950s-now, focus on how we play (consoles), [RPG Book](https://crpgbook.wordpress.com/)
- What makes a game: goals, rules, feedback, players. Q: Why do you play games? 
- Game Design Kit [Activity](https://www.cs4730.org/assets/materials/GameDesignActivity.pdf) 
- Mechanics, Dynamics, Aesthetics. MDA [paper](../files/MDA.pdf). Overview of each part with game examples (lots for aes)
- Formal Elements of Games: Fullterton GDW [Ch2](../files/GameDesignWorkshop5thEd-Fullerton.pdf#page=66): ludic structure of games, mapping to MDA.
- Let's Play Super Mario 3D: Swink Game Feel [Ch X](../files/GameFeel-Swink.pdf#page=266) 
- The Game Loop: event-driven programming, game state: player input, process actions -> npcs -> world, prepare draw -> predraw buffer -> buffer to screen 
- Procedures and Rules: Fullterton GDW [Ch3](../files/GameDesignWorkshop5thEd-Fullerton.pdf#page=90): actions vs interactions, designing actions, operational/constitutive/implicit rules; depth vs complexity
- Tutorial: Intro to Godot, nodes, scenes
- Sprite Graphics: computer graphics history, sprite sheets, animation, coordinates, scrolling, camera types
- Tutorial: sprites, assets, movement 

### Week 2: Game Design Fundamentals
implementing mechanics + tutorials (labs)

### Week 3: Game Development Introduction
ideation, prototypes, character design

### Week 4: Game Development Processes
level design, balance, playtesting
